en: The Apadāna of the Elder Veyyāvaccaka Sudhāvagga, No. 9 I was once a servant to a monk who lived in the forest. Having performed service for him, I attained the fruit of Stream-entry. By that root of merit, I have now become a monk. Through the power of that deed, I have reached the state of an Arhat. I am now free from birth, old age, and death; I have accomplished what was to be done and laid down the burden. With the taints destroyed, I have realized the goal. I am liberated through the destruction of craving. This is my final birth; there will be no further existence. Thus did I speak these verses at the foot of the Bodhi tree. May all beings be happy and well. May they be free from enmity and affliction. May they be safe and secure, and may all their wishes be fulfilled. May all beings be happy. May all beings be well. May all beings be free from enmity. May all beings be free from affliction. May all beings be safe and secure. May all beings have their wishes fulfilled. May all those who are suffering find happiness. May all those who are in distress find peace. May all those who are in pain find relief. May all those who are in fear find courage. May all beings be happy. May all beings be well. May all beings be free from enmity. May all beings be free from affliction. May all beings be safe and secure. “There was a great multitude of monks for the Blessed One Vipassī;
I am occupied with all kinds of duties,
and I have no gift to give to the Sugata, the Great Seer.
With a mind full of serene confidence, I paid homage at the feet of the Teacher in the ninety-first aeon ago.
I do not recognize a state of misery—
this is the fruit of service.
I was a king named Sucintita,
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Veyyāvaccaka speak these verses.
This is the ninth legend of the elder Veyyāvaccaka.
